response.title: How big a power station do I need to run a TV, a slow cooker and a blender for a six-hour tailgate?
response.answer:
For a six-hour tailgate running a TV, slow cooker, and blender, I'd recommend a portable power station with 2,000–2,500 Wh of battery capacity and at least 1,500 W of AC output.

The biggest factor is whether you'll keep the slow cooker running the entire six hours.

Accounting for roughly 10–15% inverter losses, you'd need approximately 1,700–2,800 Wh of rated battery capacity under these assumptions.

In practice, slow cookers cycle their heating elements on and off, so actual consumption may be lower.

What size should you buy?

1,000 Wh — Budget option

Enough if you preheat the food at home, use the slow cooker primarily to keep it warm, and have an efficient TV. Not ideal for six hours of continuous cooking.

2,000 Wh — Recommended starting point

A good balance of portability and capacity. Likely sufficient with moderate slow-cooker cycling, but not guaranteed for six hours at full heat.

3,000 Wh — More comfortable margin

Better if the slow cooker runs hot for most of the event or you want extra capacity for speakers, phones, or other accessories.

Don't overlook the blender

A blender rated at 1,000 W may briefly draw more power when starting. I'd look for a power station with:

1,500–2,000 W continuous AC output

At least 2,000 W surge capability, preferably higher

Pure sine wave AC outlets

Assumes 6 hours of TV, 6 hours of slow-cooker operation at the selected heating duty cycle, 10 minutes of blending, and 85% AC efficiency. No additional reserve included.

Two questions that would help narrow this down: What size TV are you using (32", 43", 55", etc.), and will the slow cooker be cooking food from cold or just keeping already-hot food warm?

Those details could mean the difference between needing a 1,000 Wh station and a 3,000 Wh station.

The biggest factor is whether you'll keep the slow cooker running the entire six hours.

## Estimated power needs

| Appliance | Typical power draw | Usage | Energy needed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 55" LED TV | 80–120 W | 6 hours | 480–720 Wh |
| Slow cooker | 150–250 W | 6 hours | 900–1,500 Wh |
| Blender | 500–1,000 W | 10 minutes total | 85–170 Wh |
| **Total** | | | **1,465–2,390 Wh** |

Accounting for roughly 10–15% inverter losses, you'd need approximately **1,700–2,800 Wh** of rated battery capacity under these assumptions.

In practice, slow cookers cycle their heating elements on and off, so actual consumption may be lower.

## What size should you buy?

A blender rated at 1,000 W may briefly draw more power when starting. I'd look for a power station with:

- Pure sine wave AC outlets

## Calculate your actual needs

Adjust these estimates to match your appliances.

{@body const [tv,setTv] = DIL.useState(100)}
{@body const [cooker,setCooker] = DIL.useState(200)}
{@body const [duty,setDuty] = DIL.useState(75)}
{@body const [blender,setBlender] = DIL.useState(800)}
{@body const energy = (tv*6+cooker*6*duty/100+blender/6)/0.85}

    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <label>Slow cooker heating time</label>
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{duty}%</text>
      <slider min={25} max={100} step={5} value={duty} onChange={setDuty}/>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <divider color="subtle"/>

</box>

**Two questions that would help narrow this down:** What size TV are you using (32", 43", 55", etc.), and will the slow cooker be cooking food from cold or just keeping already-hot food warm?

Those details could mean the difference between needing a 1,000 Wh station and a 3,000 Wh station.
